his_statement: strates fermées ... famille ... loc. finie ... ouvert dense
statement: A figure in a Hausdorff space E is a locally finite family of nonempty locally compact closed strata Xi, with proper included strata nowhere dense, strictly increasing manifold dimensions along inclusion, intersections unions of strata, and connected manifold residual strata Ui=Xi minus lower strata. Local finiteness makes each lower-stratum union closed and nowhere dense in Xi, so Ui is nonempty open dense.
present_status: The local-finiteness and nowhere-dense clauses together imply the asserted density; no Whitney or conical condition is assumed. This is a definition with immediate topological consequences, not an existence theorem.

statement: The open strata of a figure partition its support. Saturated subsets are unions of open strata, stable under all unions/intersections and relative complements. A closed saturated subset is a union of closed strata.
present_status: Finite descending dimension supplies a minimal stratum through each point; the frontier/intersection axiom ensures uniqueness. Local finiteness and density of each Ui imply the characterization of closed saturated subsets.

statement: The initial assertion that any figure F′ whose closed strata are among F is automatically a lower ideal is retracted. The corrected definition requires F′ to be a lower ideal. Exact example: F={S¹,{p}} with p on the circle and F′={S¹}; both are figures, F′⊂F, but F′ omits a lower stratum.
present_status: Earlier scan4; explicit correction and its own example scan28. All example hypotheses: compact Hausdorff circle; finite locally finite family; p nowhere dense; open strata {p} and S¹ minus p are connected manifolds of dimensions0,1; frontier axiom holds.

his_statement: F est connu ... Σ′F ... provient d’une figure et d’une seule
statement: Using the corrected lower-ideal notion, elementary figures are principal lower ideals of closed strata, and a figure is recovered from its elementary subfigures. Figures are locally finite compatible lower sets. In the finitist version, locally finite is replaced by finite and each principal ideal must be finite. Thus refinement and compatibility determine the family of finite figures, provided ≤ defined by their conjunction is an order and compatibility is hereditary downwards.
present_status: The characterization is a reconstruction of already given compatible pieces; it does not assert that every arbitrary closed subset of E admits a figure.

his_statement: Ces conditions sont équivalentes ... par récurrence
statement: For topological figures satisfying the initial finite-dimensional stratum hypotheses, mutual saturation of all pairwise closed-stratum intersections is equivalent to each pair of open strata being disjoint or equal. This gives compatibility, inherited by elementary subfigures and lower subfigures. For compatible figures their union and intersection are figures when the necessary local-finiteness holds.
present_status: Scan7 explains why equality of closed supports alone is insufficient, then invokes induction on dimension to recover boundaries. Set-theoretic versions later use admissibility; missing infinite-descent hypotheses must not be silently supplied.

statement: Combinatorial dimension is maximal strict-chain length in a principal stratum ideal; a nonempty figure has dimension0 iff its stratum order is discrete. Geometric dimension is the supremum of combinatorial dimensions of refinements of an elementary figure. Requiring that supremum finite is an axiom, and geometric dimension cannot increase under refinement.
present_status: Combinatorial dimension0 does not mean ordinary manifold dimension0: a connected unstratified manifold is a minimal stratum. Scan36 supremum has X where X′ is required.

statement: In the Hausdorff topological example, subdivision means refinement of the open-stratum partition with unchanged support; it is equivalent to maximality under corrected subfigure inclusion among refinements. If support is omitted, adjoining a point of the omitted region strictly extends the figure and still refines.
present_status: The point-extension proof in the scan17 margin repairs the first hesitation. The separate canonical-extension construction, by connected components of complements, is not justified by that proof.

his_statement: raffinement canonique ... Il faut prouver ... il y a un pb
statement: Proposed canonical extension of a partial refinement F′ of F: retain its open strata and add connected components of every Ui minus supp(F′). The author leaves open whether boundaries of these new pieces are unions of existing strata and whether all figure axioms hold.
present_status: This is a stronger demand than existence of some compatible refinement; tame triangulation may produce additional strata and is not a proof of this exact canonical recipe.

statement: For the abstract multistratum system, assume finite descending stratum dimension, nonempty open shadows LX°=LX minus lower shadows, and disjoint open shadows for distinct compatible multistrata. Then each figure has a partition of its shadow by its open shadows; on that figure X↦LX is injective and order reflecting. For compatible X,Y, X≤Y iff LX⊆LY iff LX°⊆LY iff LX°∩LY is nonempty; compatible shadow intersections are unions of common lower shadows.
present_status: These are conditional consequences of Cont3/4 (renumbered Cont4a,b), not deductions from refinement alone. They do not give global injectivity of X↦LX across incompatible multistrata.

statement: A proposed set-based reconstruction of all refinement and compatibility from multi-shadows is restricted and then abandoned as universal: in a pseudodisk, a place is said to require a further equivalence class of cords to the boundary, so shadows as subsets do not record all structure. The text returns to abstract multistrata.
present_status: Scan25 already warns converse axioms hold for point-based topological/tame examples, not networks; scans32–33 dated12June state the cord obstruction. No equivalence relation on cords is completely specified here, so no modern classification can be identified from this passage alone.

statement: The set-family conditions X°≠∅ and every pairwise intersection a union of smaller members are claimed to make the X° partition ⋃F. Without a descending-chain or coverage hypothesis they ensure disjointness but not coverage. Counterexample F_n=[0,1/n] for n≥1 in L=[0,1]: each residual is (1/(n+1),1/n], intersections are members, but 0 belongs to no residual.
present_status: The finite-dimensional assumption of the preceding version fixes this. The fresh set-based definition at scan26 does not yet impose it. Refined statement C-SA21-4-012.

statement: If a family of subsets has nonempty residuals and the intersection-cover condition, and every point in its union belongs to an inclusion-minimal member (e.g. the member order is well founded downwards), then the residuals partition the union. Distinct residuals are disjoint by applying the intersection-cover condition to a shared point.
present_status: Repair is independently proved in this run; not inserted into the transcription. “proved there” here refers to the proof explanation in this record, so final assembly should preserve the explicit attribution rather than imply manuscript proof.

statement: Axioms for set-based contrées distinguish set-theoretic compatibility from compatibility requiring the union to be an allowed figure. Pairwise elementary compatibility implies figure compatibility; a finite compatible family has union a figure. The stronger tentative axiom tests compatibility by equal or C-disjoint open strata, and defines point-contrées when all distinct places are compatible.
present_status: Cont′4 is expressly to be checked in forthcoming non-set examples; it is not a proved classification. Its universal role is overtaken by the cords objection.

statement: Revised abstract axioms take M with refinement order ≪ and reflexive symmetric compatibility; define ≤ as both. Require ≤ an order, hereditary compatibility, principal ideals to be figures, figures downward closed and compatible, lower subfigures and finite compatible unions allowed, plus dimensional and shadow axioms. Finite principal ideals are the extra requirement for reconstructing a finitist system from the two relations.
present_status: A versioned axiom system; numbering must be tied to scans because it changes several times.

his_statement: satisfait les conditions ... mêmes ... contrée induite
statement: A refinement-downward subset M′ inherits the displayed Cont1–4 and Fig1–4 axioms; dimensions, boundaries and shadows of its elements remain unchanged, with places L′=M′∩L. Finiteness is inherited. The refinement ideal generated by a figure is its induced contrée; under disjointness stability, all multistrata disjoint from the figure form a residual subcontrée.
present_status: The assertion is for the particular axioms listed, not every later contrée axiom. The author first raises the stability concern at scan33 and then explicitly asserts the proposition at38.

statement: Disjoint figures are compatible with empty common-stratum set; for compatible figures this is equivalent to disjoint shadows under the shadow axioms. Cont5 requires disjointness stable under arbitrary refinements, giving the same for figures. Optional Cont6 asks whether pairwise disjointness of all shadow places detects disjointness of multistrata.
present_status: The implication from shadowwise compatibility to figure disjointness is explicitly optional (Facultatif?). Empty intersection of shadows alone omits compatibility and is insufficient.

his_statement: Conditions équivalentes ... il faut un axiome
statement: For the entrywise refinement definition, maximality of a refinement F′ is equivalent to absence of a nonempty refining multistratum disjoint from F′, and to absence of a shadow place disjoint from F′, once the optional place-detection axiom and new Cont7 (different open shadows have mutually disjoint places) are imposed.
present_status: The page marks the compatibility step à vérifier and then adds the needed axiom. This criterion belongs to the refinement definition abandoned at45–46.

statement: Old Cont8 posits that common refinements of Y≪X and a submultistratum X′<X factor through the subfigure of Y consisting of pieces refining X′. It yields a shadow-intersection formula, and forces a minimal target stratum for Y to contain all of its open shadow. Hence a figure refinement induces a unique map of open strata.
present_status: The induced-refinement assertion is an added axiom; the open-shadow corollary is proved using it. Do not report the corollary without that hypothesis.

statement: The entrywise definition of figure refinement is rejected: individually refining pieces need not extend jointly to a subdivision in the pseudodisk example. The new definition makes G a refinement of F when G is a subfigure of some subdivision of F.
present_status: Scan45 has a crucial missing/ambiguous negation: it says a subdivision exists, then says it does not extend. The intended obstruction follows from surrounding prose but cannot replace the ink reading. The mathematical content is a reason for changing definitions, not a fully specified countermodel.

his_statement: relation d’ordre et pas seulement ... C′1
statement: A least figure FX through each multistratum X induces a preorder X≤Y iff FX⊆FY (equivalently X∈FY). It is a partial order only after adding separation FX≠FY for X≠Y. Then figures are lower ideals; compatibility is membership in a common figure under the pairwise-gluing axiom; the empty figure is required also when M is empty.
present_status: The margin explicitly adds C′1, preventing identification of a preorder with a poset.

statement: Original C4 would replace a subfigure G by its subdivision G′ while retaining all other multistrata: G′∪(F minus G). This is flagged false for closed/augmented strata. It is replaced by existence of a subdivision extending G′ together with G′∩F⊆G. The corrected exclusion property proves that compatible refinement is equivalent to subfigure inclusion.
present_status: Both the false explicit union and the weaker existential replacement are recorded on scan48; proof of the compatible-refinement criterion follows49. Boundary refinement generally changes the ambient multistratum itself.

statement: C5 requires subdivision to preserve all disjointness tests, equivalently virtual cosupport and support. Subdivisions of disjoint figures glue as a disjoint union; refinements of disjoint figures stay disjoint. Cosupports are closed under subdivision as well as subfigure inclusion, hence define subcontrées.
present_status: The invariance is an axiom. Its equivalent cosupport formulation is formal and is not a spatial representability theorem.

statement: C6 postulates unique restriction of a subdivision to any subfigure, characterized by strata refining that subfigure; restrictions compose both in subdividing and in restricting. C7_0 postulates extension of a subdivision of a subfigure to the whole figure. The converse claim that every subfigure of a subdivision descends is explicitly false.
present_status: A newly inserted vertex of a subdivided interval is a subfigure upstairs but is not the inverse image of an old subfigure. This is an elementary exact counterexample to descent, with finite PL intervals.

statement: Subdivisions on a cover of a figure by subfigures glue uniquely when their restrictions agree on intersections. Thus equality can be checked on elementary subfigures, and subdivision systems of disjoint sums are products of the subdivision systems of summands.
present_status: Gluing is an axiom; uniqueness/local determination and disjoint-product statement are formal consequences. Infinite covers require the admitted family/union hypotheses, not just finite PL common-subdivision facts.

statement: If G is a subfigure of F and F′ refines F in the subdivision-based sense, the largest subfigure of F′ refining G is the induced refinement and is asserted to be their infimum for refinement. Scan52 proves a version using corrected extension and restriction axioms. The new two-order proof at78–79 stops on its second lemma and refers back to manuscript p51 (=scan52).
present_status: Preserve version dependence: the reference back is real, but the later stripped two-order axiom system is explicitly questioned at86. The assertion that empty induced refinement detects disjointness remains an extra open condition at77.

statement: C1 gives nonemptiness and all bounded joins; C2 says every figure is a join of completely join-irreducible strata. Mapping a figure to its lower irreducibles is indeed an injective order embedding. However the further claim that this map sends joins to unions is false under C1+C2: the five-element diamond M3 is generated by its three irreducible atoms, but the join of two atoms has all three below it.
present_status: Every C1+C2 hypothesis is checked in outputs/computations.json. Repair C-SA21-4-027 requires completely join-prime strata (or an appropriate distributive/spatial hypothesis). Later C3 is automatic in M3 and does not fix the gap.

statement: If every figure is a join of strata that are completely join-prime for existing bounded joins, its lower-stratum map preserves those joins as unions. In the intended lower-ideal representation, subfigures of F correspond to lower subsets of its stratum poset; nonempty intersections exist and agree with stratum-set intersections. These conclusions require the strengthened representation hypothesis, not C1+C2 as printed alone.
present_status: Current-run repair. Complete join-irreducibility only tests decompositions equal to the element; complete join-primality also tests an element lying below a join.

statement: Conversely, a subset system F on M closed under bounded unions, with a least member Ax containing each x and with ∅∈F, is join-generated by the Ax. But x↦Ax need not be injective: M={a,b}, F={∅,{a,b}} satisfies every displayed condition, with Aa=Ab. Separation of points by F is the missing hypothesis.
present_status: This separation was explicitly added in the earlier formulation at scan46 (C′1), but is absent from the fresh a,b,c list. It may be a suppressed standing convention; scan check required.

statement: In the intended compatible-lower-ideal model, subfigures of a disjoint union are uniquely unions of a subfigure of each summand. The same holds for a possibly infinite bounded disjoint family. Lower subsets of M correspond to subfigure-downward, bounded-join-stable subsets of the figure system.
present_status: These are elementary set/ideal facts under the representation model; they are not consequences of the under-strengthened abstract C1+C2 alone (C-SA21-4-026).

statement: Assuming the lower-ideal model and hereditary compatibility, finite-type figures are finite unions of principal ideals generated by pairwise compatible elements. All figures are finite iff the system consists of finite compatible lower sets and each principal ideal is finite. In the finite-type version each bounded lower subset must be finitely generated.
present_status: The original wording “join of its maximal strata” does not by itself imply finite type; the interline explicitly adds finitely many. The finite classification is correct as a construction, with model hypotheses stated.

statement: In the lower-ideal model, connected figures are exactly figures whose stratum posets are connected by zigzags of comparisons; a connected subfigure of a disjoint union lies in one summand. Each figure uniquely decomposes into pairwise disjoint nonempty connected components, corresponding to components of its stratum poset.
present_status: The earlier doubt about existence (scan63) is crossed out after moving to poset components. Empty figures are called connected but not 0-connected. This convention matters for the “two of three” disjoint-sum remark.

statement: Splitting M into its comparison-connected components Mi gives an order embedding F↦(Fi) in the product of component figure systems, preserving existing joins and nonempty meets. C4 (compatibility across distinct components) implies all finite-support tuples occur; for finitely many components this is surjective; for finite-type/finite figures its image is exactly finite-support tuples. C4bis separately imposes all tuples.
present_status: This result uses the compatible-lower-ideal representation; no unrestricted-product assertion follows from pairwise compatibility alone in the infinitary setting.

statement: For symmetric disjointness ⊥, A⊥ consists of objects disjoint from every object in A. A↦A⊥⊥ is an extensive, monotone, idempotent closure; its fixed subsets form a complete lattice, with meets intersections, joins closure of unions, and ⊥ an order-reversing involution. Cosupports and supports of figure families are determined by their stratum families.
present_status: These Galois-closure facts hold for any symmetric relation. The formula at69 writes compatibility RM where disjointness is required, an important reading alarm.

statement: The complete lattice of virtual supports is conjectured Boolean, hence to have an extremally disconnected Stone spectrum; in the point-based example it is intended to identify with the powerset of the underlying point set. The general distributive law is explicitly unproved.
computation: code/computations.py: cyclic_support_lattice; all displayed structural hypotheses verified there.
present_status: A finite compatible-lower-ideal model with five vertices and five adjacent-pair multistrata supplies a counterexample under the displayed C1–C4 structure and identity subdivisions: see refined statement C-SA21-4-035. This does not refute a later strengthened axiom system not used here.

statement: Virtual supports are a complete orthocomplemented lattice when ⊥ is irreflexive and symmetric, but need not be distributive. Construct M with vertices vi and edges ei (i mod5), vi,vi+1<ei; compatibility means having a common upper bound, and figures are compatible lower sets. M is connected. Orthogonality holds only between adjacent distinct vertices. Biorthogonal closed supports give 12 elements, and {v0}∧({v1}∨{v2})={v0}, while the distributed right side is ∅.
present_status: Current-run finite countermodel. The count and distributivity witness are to be checked by the included exhaustive computation, which also tests axioms and may correct the count before finalization. Equality-only subdivision satisfies C5,C6,C7_0 and gluing when its domain is defined.

statement: A contrée is called moderated when every pair of subdivisions of a common figure admits a common subdivision; the author anticipates strengthening the condition. This is an axiom/design choice, not a theorem for arbitrary topological stratifications.
present_status: Finite PL complexes and fixed o-minimal definable families have common compatible triangulations; wild topological stratifications need extra control. None of these comparisons automatically settles the abstract pseudodisk theory.

statement: A full subcontrée is proposed to be closed under subfigures, bounded joins, and subdivisions. The author explicitly leaves undecided whether all bounded joins or only finite joins should be required.
present_status: The choice corresponds to different completions in infinitary models; in a finite figure system they coincide. No historical reason for a final choice is supplied.

statement: Refinement G≪F means G≤F′⪯F for some F′. The initial proof claims antisymmetry, then discovers an unsupported support-separation lemma and suspends antisymmetry at76. Provisional C8 prohibits loops X≤Φ⪯X and X⪯Ψ≤X for elementary X; combined with the restriction/extension machinery, scans83–84 prove antisymmetry.
present_status: Do not cite the first “order” statement without C8. The proof of transitivity uses interchange/extension of the two order relations; the precise minimal package is the next open problem.

statement: The hoped-for strict separation supp K≠supp F for every proper subfigure K<F does not follow from C1–C4 and identity subdivisions. The author gives the counterexample of all lower sets of a poset with least element0: any two nonempty lower sets intersect, so all nonempty figures have identical cosupport.
present_status: A two-element chain suffices; its nonempty ideals {0} and {0,1} have the same empty disjointness set. This is the author’s own counterexample, independently rechecked.

statement: Assuming induced-refinement infima, preservation of bounded joins under restriction, and finite descending dimension for elementary figures, an elementary refinement X≪F factors through a unique least stratum Y of F. These least targets define a monotone map on stratum posets for any figure refinement. In particular every place refining F refines a stratum of F, so shadows are unions of stratum shadows.
present_status: The proof depends on irreducibility of X and the restriction axioms. Scan80 concludes Y=Y′ where only Y≤Y′ follows; the required leastness result uses the weaker relation. Multi-shadow admissibility needs additional nonempty-shadow axioms.

statement: For two orders (subfigure and subdivision), unique induced restriction, extension, and no mixed loops are proposed to make their composite refinement relation an order, with restriction squares and ordinary intersection squares cartesian for refinement. The manuscript specifically doubts the cartesian assertions and asks for the missing hypotheses and join-preservation conditions.
present_status: A formal two-order calculus remains to be isolated; no blanket identification with an existing categorical factorization theorem is made. Earlier proof scan52 uses more structure than the stripped three conditions.

statement: A place is a nonempty figure minimal for refinement. It is necessarily elementary and minimal for subfigure inclusion. The converse, and the equivalence with merely having no proper subdivision, are not established and an attempted equivalence is crossed out. A converse is anticipated only for future contrées en boules.
present_status: Identity subdivision on a nontrivial figure system shows “no proper subdivision” is much weaker than refinement-minimality; all figures then have no proper subdivision.

statement: The final proposition claims multi-shadows form an admissible family: each stratum shadow has nonempty residual after smaller shadows, and pairwise intersections are covered by member shadows. Its proof is not present in chapter IV; these properties are revisited by the algebra-of-figures chapter.
present_status: The statement depends on the earlier place/nonempty-open-shadow axioms, which have not yet been fully restored in the last axiom list. Record as a conditional target, not unconditional consequence of just two orders.
